caption: 01 · CONDITION — Which barrier is being changed?. Use participant and field evidence to name the constraint—time, space, tools, care, legal access, production, archive, education, market, or safety—without inventing deficit narratives.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping which barrier is being changed? within Philanthropy as Continuation.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 02 · POWER — Who defines success?. Allocate governance among participants, practitioners, community authorities, staff, independent reviewers, and funder; disclose conflicts and create appeal and correction routes.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping who defines success? within Philanthropy as Continuation.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 03 · RIGHT — What do recipients retain?. Separate grant conditions, IP, name and likeness, documentation, data, confidentiality, cultural knowledge, publication, archive, and post-program access.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping what do recipients retain? within Philanthropy as Continuation.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 04 · CONTINUE — What remains when funding stops?. Plan unrestricted assets, maintained tools, open or governed curricula, participant networks, preserved records, successor funding, and an ethical closure route.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping what remains when funding stops? within Philanthropy as Continuation.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
